title: When the Majority is Wrong: Modeling Annotator Disagreement for Subjective Tasks

bias_targets.methodology: Predicting individual annotator ratings of potentially offensive text using annotator race as a feature, and evaluating the target offense error for statements targeting specific racial groups.
Predicting annotator ratings based on gender identity (including cisgender, transgender, and nonbinary annotators), and evaluating prediction error across these groups.
Predicting annotator ratings based on the self-reported importance of religion, and evaluating the target offense error for texts targeting religious groups or non-believers.
Evaluating the mean absolute error (MAE) of predicting individual annotator ratings based on their political leaning (conservative, independent, liberal).
Predicting individual annotator ratings based on age, and evaluating the prediction error for offensive text targeting specific age groups (e.g., teens, millennials).
Evaluating the mean absolute error (MAE) of predicting annotator ratings based on their education level (e.g., less than high school, doctoral degree).
Predicting individual annotator ratings on hate speech and offensive text based on annotators' self-identified LGBT status.
Evaluating the rating prediction error for offensive texts explicitly targeting specific nationalities (e.g., Syrian, Brazilian, Australian, Russian).
